subject: Renewal + Dedicated expansion: request for credit approval for additional GPU pools
messages:

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Renewal & capacity increase — initial proposal

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. To recap: BrightEdge is approaching renewal (Aug 1) and wants to consolidate into a renewed Dedicated contract with an expanded reserved pool — moving from today’s 16 GPUs to a 40-GPU committed pool (mix of A10G/RTX equivalents) to support your new batch inference pipelines.

Key asks from your side: 24-month term, guaranteed 3PPS throughput target for inference, and a request for a commercial concession (one-time onboarding credit or percent discount) tied to the expansion. Attached is an updated quote and SOW with the capacity line items (BrightEdge-Dedicated-Quote-v3.pdf, SOW_BrightEdge_Dedicated.docx).

Can you confirm procurement timelines and whether procurement needs a formal exec approval for any non-standard credit? We’ll need that for internal approvals.

Next steps I propose:
- Procurement confirmation of PO timing and contract recipient
- I’ll escalate to pricing/finance for a one-time credit proposal and confirm SLA wording with Neha
- We’ll prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment once terms are agreed

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments. Procurement timeline is tight — we need an executed amendment by 07/28 to avoid interim overages. Finance will expect to see any credits or discounts reflected clearly on the quote and in the SOW.

From our side, the ask is straightforward: some commercial concession tied to the 24-month commit (we proposed 15% off list on the expanded capacity or a one-time credit worth 3 months of pool fees). Also need explicit throughput SLA in the SOW.

If an executive-level approval is required on your side for the credit, please advise who you’ll loop in and expected timing.

—Sanjay

Marissa / Markus —

Looping you in for visibility and quick decisioning. BrightEdge is asking for a credit tied to a 24-month renewal with a large Dedicated pool increase (16 -> 40 GPUs). Customer is flexible between a 15% discount on the incremental capacity or an equivalent one-time credit (approx $120k). They need final terms signed by 07/28.

Financials: this upsell should increase ARR substantially; model shows ~45% uplift in committed spend once renewed. We can propose a structured concession: smaller one-time credit + extended committed term. Neha, can you confirm the SLA/throughput guarantee wording we can commit to?

Asking Marissa for approval to offer a blended concession (example below) and sign-off to route to DocuSign:
- One-time credit: 10% of the first-year committed spend for the incremental pool
- Price lock: commit to current per-GPU rate for first 12 months of the 24-month term
- SLA: 99.5% availability, throughput baseline with credits tied to missed targets

If you approve, I’ll get marketing/AE co-term paperwork ready and send the updated quote to procurement.

—Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: BrightEdge renewal — credit request (needs exec sign-off)

Thanks for the context. Quick decision: approve a commercial concession but limit downside. Approve the following, conditional on Legal sign-off on amendment language and Finance confirming P&L impact:

Approved concession (final):
- One-time credit equal to 10% of year-one committed spend for the incremental capacity (applied at signing)
- Additional price protection: lock current per-GPU list rate for first 12 months of the new 24-month term on the expanded pool only
- No ongoing percent discount after first 12 months; full list thereafter

Also require:
- Procurement must accept revised SOW with SLA language drafted by Neha (we will not provide custom platform engineering work — SLA will cover availability and throughput guarantees tied to provisioning and autoscale limits)
- Deal to be executed via amendment + PO; credit shows as one-line credit on invoice

Markus: please prepare simple finance note (expected ARR uplift, one-time revenue reduction, tax treatment) so Rishi can present this to the customer. I want the DocuSign envelope ready by 07/18 so we have margin before 07/28.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: BrightEdge renewal — SLA and throughput wording

Rishi / team —

I drafted the SLA clause and appended an operational appendix for capacity provisioning and scaling windows. Summary of key points I can commit to in the amendment:
- Availability: 99.5% monthly uptime on Dedicated pool (credit ladder for missed availability)
- Throughput baseline: specify measured requests-per-second (RPS) baseline per GPU class; provide 14-day ramp for initial workload profile adjustments
- Autoscale / burst: allow burst capacity up to 20% of committed pool for short-lived spikes (billing at overage rate unless we consume reserved burst credits)

I’ve attached the language I recommend to the SOW. If Finance/Legal sign-off is in place I can insert this into the final SOW and we can circulate to procurement.

—Neha
Head of Product Reliability, Redwood Inference
